"""Outbound Files integration for the Files & Data node family (#1407).

This is workflow-svc's SECOND outbound hop to another vertical, after
:mod:`workflow_svc.dialogue` (#1394). Read that package's docstring first —
the four-gate auth posture is the same shape and is not repeated in full
here. What differs is written down below, because none of it is inferable
from the client code.

**Who calls.** ``workflow-svc-worker``, not workflow-svc. A workflow run is
dispatched over JetStream long after the user who started it went away, so
the worker mints its own OIDC ``client_credentials`` token
(:mod:`workflow_svc.serviceauth`, shared with the Dialogue hop and the Media
family's studio-svc hop).

**The four gates, as they apply here:**

1. *mTLS* — dials via ``omnicore_svc_runtime.mtls.build_channel``.
2. *aud* — the ``workflow-svc-worker`` realm client gains an
   ``audience-files-svc-via-workflow-svc-worker`` protocol mapper, so its
   token is minted with ``aud=[workflow-svc, studio-svc, dialogue-svc,
   files-svc]``. pyjwt treats a multi-valued ``aud`` as a membership test, so
   one token still serves every target.
3. *azp* — ``FILES_SVC_ALLOWED_AZP`` (platform/compose/files-svc.yml) gains
   ``workflow-svc-worker``.
4. *tenant* — a ``client_credentials`` token carries no ``org_id``. The
   ``tenant:any`` realm role (already granted to
   ``service-account-workflow-svc-worker`` for the Dialogue hop) is what lets
   files-svc's interceptor ADOPT ``x-tenant-id`` as the caller's effective
   org. Without the role, files-svc rejects a blank-org_id token that names a
   tenant — that is F31, and it stays intact for every token lacking the
   grant.

**A fifth thing, specific to this hop: the actor.** Every call here forwards
``x-user-id`` carrying ``workflow.executions.created_by`` — the UUID of the
person who STARTED the run — and not the service account. Attributing a write
to the initiator is the honest answer to "who saved this file", and the
literal string ``workflow-svc-worker`` (what ``NodeContext.user_id`` carries)
could not satisfy ``files.documents.uploaded_by``, which is ``UUID NOT NULL``.
``NodeContext.initiator_user_id`` exists for exactly this.

**files-svc reads that header as of #2922, so the gate is effective.** It
adopts ``x-user-id`` as the acting user for a caller holding ``tenant:any``,
symmetrically with how it already adopts ``x-tenant-id``, and validates the
adopted id against its own org-membership projection. Two consequences, both
of which reverse decisions #2918 made:

1. Attribution lands on the initiator. ``documents.uploaded_by`` and
   ``deleted_by`` name the person whose run wrote or superseded the document,
   not ``service-account-workflow-svc-worker``.
2. A run reads what the initiator reads, PRIVATE corpora included — so
   ``workflow-bff``'s corpus picker no longer filters to TEAM and its document
   routes no longer refuse a non-TEAM collection. See ``ListCorpora``.

What did NOT become unnecessary: a corpus PRIVATE to a DIFFERENT user is
still invisible, reachable through a stale saved canvas or a direct API call.
``client._NOT_FOUND_HINT`` and :meth:`FilesClient.corpus_is_readable` still
disambiguate that, and files-svc still answers an invisible corpus with an
empty ``List`` rather than an error.

**Bytes do not go over gRPC.** ``DocumentService.Upload`` takes a
bucket-relative MinIO key, not content: "files stream through files-bff to
MinIO; this RPC just receives the metadata + MinIO object key" (see
``platform/proto/omnicore/files/document/v1/document.proto``). So a caller
that wants to save content MUST put the object itself first. files-bff's
Upload handler does precisely that, and :class:`FilesClient` is a second
caller of the same contract rather than a new pattern — including the
compensating ``DeleteObject`` when ``Upload`` is then rejected, so a
failed save leaves no orphaned object with no owning row.

**Reads do not all go over gRPC either.** ``document_query`` searches the
Qdrant collection files-svc writes rather than calling files-svc at all,
because files-svc exposes no search RPC and the chunk payload was
deliberately given a ``text`` field so cross-vertical readers could do this.
That read lives in :mod:`workflow_svc.files.search`; see the design doc §4
and range-svc's ``embedding/qdrant_client.py``, which calls the same read
"the architecture-blessed cross-vertical read".

``addr=""`` returns a DISABLED client: every method raises
:class:`FilesClientError` without touching the network. That is the state a
worker boots into when ``FILES_SVC_ADDR`` or
``WORKFLOW_SVC_WORKER_CLIENT_SECRET`` is unset, and it fails exactly ONE node
per run rather than the whole worker.
"""

from workflow_svc.files.client import (
    DocumentMeta,
    FilesClient,
    FilesClientError,
    UploadResult,
)
from workflow_svc.files.search import ChunkHit, FilesChunkSearch, FilesChunkSearchError

__all__ = [
    "ChunkHit",
    "DocumentMeta",
    "FilesChunkSearch",
    "FilesChunkSearchError",
    "FilesClient",
    "FilesClientError",
    "UploadResult",
]

"""FilesClient — workflow-svc-worker's outbound gRPC client to files-svc.

Files & Data node family (#1407). Read :mod:`workflow_svc.files`'s package
docstring first: it holds the five-gate auth posture (four shared with the
Dialogue hop, plus the initiator-actor rule) and the reason bytes do not
travel over gRPC. None of that is inferable from this file alone.

Scope is exactly what the five nodes need, and no more:

- ``get_document`` — metadata only. ``load_document`` calls it BEFORE
  streaming so an oversized document costs one RPC instead of 50 MB of
  transfer (design §5).
- ``list_documents`` — every document in a corpus, paged to exhaustion.
  This is what scopes ``document_query`` to a corpus: the Qdrant chunk payload
  carries a ``document_id`` but no ``corpus_id``, so the corpus has to be
  turned into a document-id set first (design §4).
- ``get_raw_file`` — the only raw-bytes surface files-svc has.
- ``save_document`` — MinIO put + ``Upload``, with the compensating delete.
- ``trash_document`` — the second half of Save to Table's append (design
  §6.4). Trash, never Purge: a mis-wired workflow must be undoable from the
  Files UI.

``addr=""`` (or no token source) returns a DISABLED client: every method
raises :class:`FilesClientError` without touching the network.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Protocol

import grpc
from omnicore.files.corpus.v1 import corpus_pb2, corpus_pb2_grpc
from omnicore.files.document.v1 import document_pb2, document_pb2_grpc
from omnicore_svc_runtime.mtls import MTLSConfig, build_channel

#: Bound every unary RPC. A hung files-svc must not pin the worker on one
#: node for longer than the engine's own 30 s per-node dispatch timeout, which
#: would make the node's failure read as an engine timeout instead of a Files
#: one.
_UNARY_TIMEOUT_S = 20.0

#: Streaming a document can legitimately take longer than a unary read — up to
#: `MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES` of it — but still has to fit inside the engine's
#: per-node budget, so this is deliberately under it.
_RAW_FILE_TIMEOUT_S = 25.0

#: `DocumentService.List` caps `limit` at 200 server-side (document.proto). Ask
#: for the cap rather than the default 50 so a large corpus costs a quarter of
#: the round trips.
_LIST_PAGE_SIZE = 200

#: Hard stop on the paging loop in `list_documents`. A corpus with more
#: documents than this cannot be searched exhaustively in one node run, and
#: silently searching a prefix would make `document_query` quietly wrong on
#: big corpora. The caller surfaces the truncation instead.
_MAX_LIST_PAGES = 50


class FilesClientError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the Files hop cannot be completed.

    Covers "this client was never configured", "files-svc answered with an
    error", and "the object store rejected the write". Every executor converts
    it into a ``NodeExecutionError`` so the run records ONE failed node rather
    than a crashed worker.
    """


#: Appended to a NOT_FOUND from files-svc, which is genuinely ambiguous here
#: and was actively misleading in review.
#:
#: files-svc gates every client-facing document read on
#: ``_CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE`` — ``visibility = 'TEAM' OR created_by =
#: app.current_user_id`` — so a document in a collection the acting user did
#: not create and that is not shared is indistinguishable from a deleted one:
#: both answer NOT_FOUND.
#:
#: #2922 narrowed which collections that covers but did not remove the
#: ambiguity. files-svc now binds ``app.current_user_id`` from the
#: ``x-user-id`` this client forwards, so the acting user is the run's
#: initiator and their OWN private collections are readable. Someone ELSE's
#: private collection still is not — reachable through a canvas saved by a
#: colleague, a shared workflow, or a direct API call — and a bare "document
#: not found" would still send an operator looking for a deletion that never
#: happened.
_NOT_FOUND_HINT = (
    " — either it was deleted, or it lives in a collection you cannot open: a "
    "run reads as the person who started it, so another user's private "
    "collection is invisible to it. Documents a shared workflow reads should "
    "be in a shared (TEAM) collection."
)


#: Appended when a WRITE is rejected because its target corpus is not visible.
#:
#: The write path expresses the same invisibility as the read path but with a
#: different status and a worse message. ``DocumentService.Upload`` pre-checks
#: ``GET_CORPUS`` — which carries the same ``_CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE`` — and
#: aborts FAILED_PRECONDITION with ``corpus_id <uuid> not found in this org``.
#: That sentence is wrong from the operator's side whenever the cause is
#: visibility: the collection IS in their org.
#:
#: Found while re-checking the read-path fix from review on PR #2918. The same
#: defect, one status code over. Since #2922 the initiator's own private
#: collections are writable, so what reaches here is a collection belonging to
#: someone else — which the wording now says.
_CORPUS_NOT_WRITABLE_HINT = (
    " — if that collection exists but belongs to another user and is private, "
    "a run cannot write to it: a run acts as the person who started it. Save "
    "to your own collection or a shared (TEAM) one."
)


def _rpc_message(action: str, exc: grpc.aio.AioRpcError) -> str:
    """Render one failed RPC as a node-failure reason.

    NOT_FOUND gets :data:`_NOT_FOUND_HINT`; every other code speaks for itself
    and is passed through unchanged rather than being second-guessed.
    """
    detail = exc.details() or exc.code().name
    if exc.code() is grpc.StatusCode.NOT_FOUND:
        return f"{action}: {detail}{_NOT_FOUND_HINT}"
    return f"{action}: {detail}"


def _upload_message(exc: grpc.aio.AioRpcError) -> str:
    """Render a failed ``Upload`` as a node-failure reason.

    Separate from :func:`_rpc_message` because the ambiguity is different on
    this path: files-svc answers FAILED_PRECONDITION (not NOT_FOUND) for a
    corpus the caller cannot see, so the read hint would never fire and the
    write hint must not leak onto unrelated preconditions. Only that one code
    is decorated; everything else passes through.
    """
    detail = exc.details() or exc.code().name
    if exc.code() is grpc.StatusCode.FAILED_PRECONDITION:
        return f"document upload failed: {detail}{_CORPUS_NOT_WRITABLE_HINT}"
    return f"document upload failed: {detail}"


class TokenSourceLike(Protocol):
    """Structural type for the injected token source (ServiceAccountTokenSource
    in production; a fake in tests)."""

    async def get_token(self) -> str: ...


class ObjectStoreLike(Protocol):
    """The two S3 operations ``save_document`` needs.

    A Protocol rather than a concrete aiobotocore client so tests inject a
    double without a live MinIO, and so the compensating-delete path is
    exercisable. Matches aiobotocore's own async client surface.
    """

    async def put_object(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Any: ...
    async def delete_object(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Any: ...


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class DocumentMeta:
    """The subset of ``files.document.v1.Document`` this family reads."""

    id: str
    filename: str
    mime_type: str
    size_bytes: int
    corpus_id: str
    #: Pipeline state of the document's most recent ingest job — "complete",
    #: "failed", one of the in-flight states, or "" when no job exists.
    #: `document_query` reports it so a corpus that has not finished ingesting
    #: explains its own empty result set instead of looking broken.
    ingest_status: str


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class UploadResult:
    """What ``save_document`` learned from files-svc about the new row."""

    document_id: str
    filename: str
    mime_type: str
    size_bytes: int
    #: files-svc enqueues parse/chunk/embed on Upload and returns the job id.
    #: Carried through to the node's `result` because saving a document is
    #: only the START of ingest — a workflow that saves then queries needs
    #: this to know when the document became searchable.
    ingest_job_id: str


def _mtls_cfg_from_env() -> MTLSConfig:
    """Same ``MTLS_*_FILE`` env vars the inbound server reads (P0-05) — this is
    the outbound half of the same east-west posture."""
    return MTLSConfig(
        os.environ.get("MTLS_CERT_FILE", ""),
        os.environ.get("MTLS_KEY_FILE", ""),
        os.environ.get("MTLS_CA_FILE", ""),
    )


def _document_meta(doc: Any) -> DocumentMeta:
    """Map a wire ``Document`` onto :class:`DocumentMeta`."""
    return DocumentMeta(
        id=str(doc.id),
        filename=str(doc.filename),
        mime_type=str(doc.mime_type),
        size_bytes=int(doc.size_bytes),
        corpus_id=str(doc.corpus_id),
        ingest_status=str(doc.ingest_status),
    )


@dataclass(slots=True)
class FilesClient:
    """Thin wrapper around files-svc's ``DocumentServiceStub`` plus the object
    store its Upload contract requires the caller to write to.

    Parameters:
    - ``addr`` — files-svc gRPC dial target (e.g. ``"files-svc:50051"``).
      Empty disables the client.
    - ``token_source`` — mints the bearer JWT files-svc's AuthInterceptor
      requires on every RPC. ``None`` disables the client.
    - ``bucket`` — the files-svc MinIO bucket. Blank disables WRITES only:
      reads still work, and `save_to_file` fails that one node with a reason
      naming the missing config.
    - ``object_store`` — an :class:`ObjectStoreLike`. ``None`` likewise
      disables writes only.
    - ``stub`` — optional injected ``DocumentServiceStub``-shaped double.
    """

    addr: str
    token_source: TokenSourceLike | None
    bucket: str = ""
    object_store: ObjectStoreLike | None = None
    stub: Any | None = None
    #: ``CorpusServiceStub``, used ONLY by :meth:`corpus_is_readable`. Shares
    #: the one channel; injectable separately so a test can drive the probe
    #: without a document stub.
    corpus_stub: Any | None = None
    _channel: grpc.aio.Channel | None = field(init=False, default=None)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.stub is None and self.addr:
            self._channel, _ = build_channel(self.addr, _mtls_cfg_from_env())
            self.stub = document_pb2_grpc.DocumentServiceStub(self._channel)  # type: ignore[no-untyped-call]
            if self.corpus_stub is None:
                self.corpus_stub = corpus_pb2_grpc.CorpusServiceStub(self._channel)  # type: ignore[no-untyped-call]

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """True when a stub AND a token source are both configured.

        Both halves are required: an addr with no token source could only ever
        produce UNAUTHENTICATED, and a token source with no addr has nowhere to
        send it. Refusing to half-enable keeps this an honest single predicate.
        """
        return self.stub is not None and self.token_source is not None

    @property
    def writable(self) -> bool:
        """True when this client can also SAVE — i.e. it has somewhere to put
        the bytes ``Upload`` will then register.

        Deliberately separate from :attr:`enabled`: a worker configured for
        files-svc but not for MinIO can still run every read node, and only
        `save_to_file` / `save_to_table` need to fail.
        """
        return self.enabled and bool(self.bucket) and self.object_store is not None

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the gRPC channel and the token source's HTTP client."""
        if self._channel is not None:
            await self._channel.close()
        if self.token_source is not None:
            closer = getattr(self.token_source, "close", None)
            if closer is not None:
                await closer()

    async def _metadata(self, *, org_id: str, user_id: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
        """Build the outbound metadata for one RPC.

        ``x-tenant-id`` is the tenant this run belongs to; files-svc ADOPTS it
        as the caller's effective org because the worker's token carries the
        ``tenant:any`` grant and no ``org_id`` of its own.

        ``x-user-id`` is the UUID of the person who STARTED the run, not the
        service account. files-svc ADOPTS it as the acting user under the same
        ``tenant:any`` grant, so everything it derives from the acting user
        follows this value: ``documents.uploaded_by``, ``deleted_by``, and the
        ``app.current_user_id`` GUC that decides corpus visibility.

        That adoption is #2922, and it is what makes this header load-bearing
        rather than decorative. Before it, files-svc derived the acting user
        from the token SUBJECT and ignored this header entirely, so every
        run-authored document was owned by the worker's service account and a
        run could read ``TEAM`` corpora only. Both halves are now the
        initiator's.

        Sending a ``x-user-id`` that is not a member of ``org_id`` is
        PERMISSION_DENIED at files-svc, not a silent fallback to the service
        account — so pass ``executions.created_by``, never
        ``NodeContext.user_id`` (the service-account name).
        """
        if self.token_source is None:  # pragma: no cover - guarded by `enabled`
            raise FilesClientError("files client is not configured")
        token = await self.token_source.get_token()
        metadata = [
            ("authorization", f"Bearer {token}"),
            ("x-tenant-id", org_id),
            ("x-actor-type", "service"),
        ]
        if user_id:
            metadata.append(("x-user-id", user_id))
        return metadata

    def _require_enabled(self) -> None:
        if not self.enabled:
            raise FilesClientError(
                "the Files integration is not configured on this worker "
                "(FILES_SVC_ADDR / WORKFLOW_SVC_WORKER_CLIENT_SECRET)"
            )

    async def get_document(self, document_id: str, *, org_id: str, user_id: str) -> DocumentMeta:
        """Fetch one document's metadata. Raises on a missing/forbidden id."""
        self._require_enabled()
        assert self.stub is not None  # narrowed by `enabled`
        metadata = await self._metadata(org_id=org_id, user_id=user_id)
        try:
            resp = await self.stub.Get(
                document_pb2.GetRequest(document_id=document_id),
                metadata=metadata,
                timeout=_UNARY_TIMEOUT_S,
            )
        except grpc.aio.AioRpcError as exc:
            raise FilesClientError(_rpc_message("document lookup failed", exc)) from exc
        return _document_meta(resp.document)

    async def list_documents(
        self,
        corpus_id: str,
        *,
        org_id: str,
        user_id: str,
        max_pages: int = _MAX_LIST_PAGES,
    ) -> tuple[list[DocumentMeta], bool]:
        """Page every document in a corpus, across folders.

        ``all_folders=True`` deliberately: a corpus-wide search must not be
        silently limited to corpus-root documents, which is what the
        ``folder_id``-unset default means (see document.proto's ListRequest).

        Returns ``(documents, truncated)``. ``truncated`` is True when
        ``max_pages`` was exhausted with a cursor still outstanding — the
        caller surfaces it rather than searching a prefix and reporting a
        complete answer.
        """
        self._require_enabled()
        assert self.stub is not None  # narrowed by `enabled`
        metadata = await self._metadata(org_id=org_id, user_id=user_id)
        out: list[DocumentMeta] = []
        cursor = ""
        for _ in range(max(1, max_pages)):
            try:
                resp = await self.stub.List(
                    document_pb2.ListRequest(
                        corpus_id=corpus_id,
                        cursor=cursor,
                        limit=_LIST_PAGE_SIZE,
                        all_folders=True,
                    ),
                    metadata=metadata,
                    timeout=_UNARY_TIMEOUT_S,
                )
            except grpc.aio.AioRpcError as exc:
                raise FilesClientError(_rpc_message("document list failed", exc)) from exc
            out.extend(_document_meta(d) for d in resp.documents)
            cursor = str(resp.next_cursor)
            if not cursor:
                return out, False
        return out, True

    async def get_raw_file(
        self, document_id: str, *, org_id: str, user_id: str
    ) -> tuple[bytes, str, str]:
        """Stream a document's full raw bytes.

        Returns ``(data, mime_type, filename)``. The first frame of the stream
        is metadata and every later frame is a data chunk — see
        ``GetRawFileResponse``'s ``oneof``.

        An empty document is NOT an error here: a zero-byte CSV is a real
        (if useless) table, and the caller is better placed to decide whether
        emptiness matters than this transport wrapper is.
        """
        self._require_enabled()
        assert self.stub is not None  # narrowed by `enabled`
        metadata = await self._metadata(org_id=org_id, user_id=user_id)
        chunks: list[bytes] = []
        mime_type = ""
        filename = ""
        try:
            call = self.stub.GetRawFile(
                document_pb2.GetRawFileRequest(document_id=document_id),
                metadata=metadata,
                timeout=_RAW_FILE_TIMEOUT_S,
            )
            async for frame in call:
                if frame.WhichOneof("frame") == "metadata":
                    mime_type = str(frame.metadata.mime_type)
                    filename = str(frame.metadata.filename)
                else:
                    chunks.append(frame.data)
        except grpc.aio.AioRpcError as exc:
            # Same NOT_FOUND ambiguity as the unary reads above — a document in
            # a PRIVATE collection and a deleted one are indistinguishable from
            # here.
            raise FilesClientError(_rpc_message("document download failed", exc)) from exc
        except grpc.RpcError as exc:
            # Broader net for a streaming call: not every failure on this path
            # carries a status code (a transport drop mid-stream does not), so
            # this arm keeps the raw repr rather than pretending to classify it.
            raise FilesClientError(f"document download failed: {exc}") from exc
        return b"".join(chunks), mime_type, filename

    async def corpus_is_readable(self, corpus_id: str, *, org_id: str, user_id: str) -> bool:
        """Can a workflow RUN read this collection at all?

        Exists because "this collection is empty" and "this collection is
        invisible to me" are the same answer from ``DocumentService.List``:
        files-svc gates it on ``_CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE`` but returns an
        EMPTY LIST rather than an error, so an unreadable corpus looks exactly
        like an empty one. Without this, ``document_query`` reported "no
        results" for a collection the run was never allowed to see — the
        quietest failure of the three in this family.

        #2922 shrank the set this catches without emptying it: the acting user
        is now the run's initiator, so their own private collections read
        fine, but ANOTHER user's private collection still comes back empty —
        reachable through a colleague's saved canvas, a shared workflow, or a
        direct API call. Keep the probe.

        Deliberately called ONLY on the empty path, so the ordinary case costs
        nothing.

        Returns False on NOT_FOUND, which is what files-svc answers for both
        "no such corpus" and "not visible to you" — the caller wants the same
        message either way. Any OTHER failure RAISES rather than returning
        False: reporting "your collection is private" because files-svc was
        briefly unreachable would be its own wrong answer.
        """
        self._require_enabled()
        if self.corpus_stub is None:
            # An injected document stub with no corpus stub (older test
            # doubles). Treat as readable: this probe exists to IMPROVE an
            # error message, and must never manufacture one of its own.
            return True
        metadata = await self._metadata(org_id=org_id, user_id=user_id)
        try:
            await self.corpus_stub.Get(
                corpus_pb2.GetRequest(corpus_id=corpus_id),
                metadata=metadata,
                timeout=_UNARY_TIMEOUT_S,
            )
        except grpc.aio.AioRpcError as exc:
            if exc.code() is grpc.StatusCode.NOT_FOUND:
                return False
            raise FilesClientError(_rpc_message("collection lookup failed", exc)) from exc
        return True

    @staticmethod
    def _object_key(org_id: str) -> str:
        """Build the bucket-relative MinIO key for a new document.

        Mirrors files-bff's ``document.go`` byte-for-byte in SHAPE
        (``org/<orgId>/doc/<unix-nanos>``) and, as there, deliberately omits
        the filename: it is unsanitized input (path separators, "..", control
        characters, unicode tricks) and files-svc stores the display name
        separately on ``documents.filename``. Key and display name stay
        decoupled.
        """
        return f"org/{org_id}/doc/{time.time_ns()}"

    async def save_document(
        self,
        *,
        org_id: str,
        user_id: str,
        corpus_id: str,
        filename: str,
        mime_type: str,
        content: bytes,

"""MinioObjectStore — the object-store half of the Files save path (#1407).

``DocumentService.Upload`` takes a bucket-relative object KEY and never
bytes: "files stream through files-bff to MinIO; this RPC just receives the
metadata + MinIO object key" (document.proto). So a caller that wants to save
content must put the object itself first, which is exactly what files-bff's
Upload handler does. :class:`MinioObjectStore` is the workflow worker's half
of that same contract, and nothing more — two operations, both used only by
``save_to_file`` and ``save_to_table``.

Modelled directly on ``files_svc.minio_client.MinIOClient``, including the
part that is easy to get wrong: ``aiobotocore``'s ``create_client`` returns an
async CONTEXT MANAGER, not a client, so its ``__aenter__``/``__aexit__`` have
to be driven explicitly to keep one client alive across many calls. Opening a
fresh client per call would turn a workflow that writes N files into N TLS
connection establishments.

The client is opened LAZILY, on first use, for two reasons: the factory that
constructs this object is synchronous (an executor is a module-level function
with no async init point), and a worker whose runs never reach a save node
should never open an S3 session at all.

``signature_version="s3v4"`` + path-style addressing mirror files-svc's own
config. MinIO requires path style — virtual-host addressing would resolve
``<bucket>.minio`` as a hostname, which does not exist on the compose network.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any


@dataclass
class MinioObjectStore:
    """Long-lived async S3 client exposing just ``put_object`` / ``delete_object``.

    Satisfies :class:`workflow_svc.files.client.ObjectStoreLike` structurally,
    so ``FilesClient`` depends on the two methods rather than on aiobotocore.
    """

    endpoint_url: str
    access_key: str
    secret_key: str
    secure: bool = False
    region: str = "us-east-1"
    _session: Any = field(default=None, init=False, repr=False)
    _client_cm: Any = field(default=None, init=False, repr=False)
    _client: Any = field(default=None, init=False, repr=False)

    async def _ensure_client(self) -> Any:
        """Open the underlying aiobotocore client on first use."""
        if self._client is not None:
            return self._client
        import aiobotocore.session
        from botocore.config import Config

        if self._session is None:
            self._session = aiobotocore.session.get_session()
        # See the module docstring: this is an async context manager, driven
        # explicitly so one client survives many calls and is torn down in
        # `close()`.
        self._client_cm = self._session.create_client(
            "s3",
            endpoint_url=self.endpoint_url,
            aws_access_key_id=self.access_key,
            aws_secret_access_key=self.secret_key,
            use_ssl=self.secure,
            # MinIO ignores the region but botocore requires one to sign.
            region_name=self.region,
            config=Config(
                signature_version="s3v4",
                s3={"addressing_style": "path"},
            ),
        )
        self._client = await self._client_cm.__aenter__()
        return self._client

    async def put_object(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        """Write one object. Keyword arguments are botocore's own."""
        s3 = await self._ensure_client()
        return await s3.put_object(**kwargs)

    async def delete_object(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        """Delete one object — the compensating half of a rejected upload."""
        s3 = await self._ensure_client()
        return await s3.delete_object(**kwargs)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Tear the client down. Idempotent; safe on a never-opened store."""
        if self._client_cm is not None:
            await self._client_cm.__aexit__(None, None, None)
        self._client_cm = None
        self._client = None

"""FilesChunkSearch — semantic search over the chunk collection files-svc writes.

Files & Data node family (#1407), backing the Document Query node (#1408).
Read the design doc's §4 before changing this: the choice to read Qdrant
rather than call files-svc is the load-bearing decision of the epic, and it
is not obvious from here that it is a sanctioned pattern rather than a
shortcut.

The short version. files-svc ingests, chunks and embeds documents into a
per-tenant Qdrant collection, and exposes **no search RPC at all** — the only
``search_documents`` in the platform is a declared tool name in
``agents-svc/internal/registry`` with ``JSONSchema: "{}"`` and no
implementation. What files-svc DOES do is store the chunk text in the Qdrant
point payload specifically so other verticals can read it: see
``files_svc.worker.qdrant_client.upsert_chunk``, whose docstring says the text
is there "so that cross-vertical readers (range-svc RAG retrieval) can pull
grounding text straight from Qdrant with no files-svc gRPC hop". range-svc's
``embedding/qdrant_client.search_chunks_by_vector`` is that reader, and calls
it "the architecture-blessed cross-vertical read; range-svc never calls
files-svc gRPC". This module is the second such reader.

**files-svc owns and writes this collection; workflow-svc only reads it.**
Nothing here creates, upserts into or deletes from it, and nothing should.

Two couplings this file cannot avoid and therefore names loudly:

1. **The collection name** must match
   ``files_svc.worker.qdrant_client.Qdrant.chunks_collection`` exactly.
2. **The embedding model** must be the one files-svc embedded the chunks with,
   or the query lands in a different vector space and retrieval returns noise
   that *looks* like results. ``WORKFLOW_FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL`` therefore
   defaults to files-svc's own ``FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL`` default
   (``nomic-embed-text:latest``) — NOT to workflow's gen-model pin. range-svc
   carries the identical ``RANGE_FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL`` for the identical
   reason.

payload carries ``org_id``, ``chunk_id``, ``document_id`` and ``text`` — no
``corpus_id``. So the caller resolves the corpus to its document ids (via
``FilesClient.list_documents``) and this module filters ``MatchAny`` over
them, exactly as range-svc filters to a run's attached documents.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

import httpx
from qdrant_client import AsyncQdrantClient, models

#: files-svc's own default (``FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL``). See the module
#: docstring: matching it is a correctness requirement, not a preference.
DEFAULT_FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL = "nomic-embed-text:latest"

#: Bound the embedding call. Long enough for a cold model load on the shared
#: gateway, short enough to stay inside the engine's 30 s per-node budget.
_EMBED_TIMEOUT_S = 20.0

#: Cap on the query text handed to the embedder. Legacy's document_query
#: truncated at 512 characters before embedding for the same reason: an
#: embedding model has a fixed context, and silently feeding it more produces a
#: vector for a prefix while implying the whole query was used.
MAX_QUERY_CHARS = 512


class FilesChunkSearchError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the query could not be embedded or the search could not run.

    Deliberately NOT raised for an empty result set, a collection that does
    not exist yet, or a corpus whose documents have not finished ingesting —
    all three are legitimate "no matches" answers, and `exec_document_query`
    reports them as an empty `results` list rather than a failed node.
    """


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ChunkHit:
    """One search result — a chunk of one document, with its similarity."""

    document_id: str
    text: str
    #: Qdrant's cosine score for the collection's configured distance. Higher
    #: is nearer. Passed through verbatim rather than rescaled: legacy's node
    #: did `1 - score` arithmetic that assumed a DISTANCE, and this
    #: collection is configured with `Distance.COSINE`, where the score is
    #: already a similarity. Rescaling it would invert the ranking.
    score: float


@dataclass(slots=True)
class FilesChunkSearch:
    """Read-only searcher over ``files_chunks_{org_id}``.

    Parameters:
    - ``qdrant_url`` — e.g. ``"http://qdrant:6333"``. Empty disables.
    - ``litellm_url`` / ``litellm_api_key`` — the embeddings gateway.
      A blank ``litellm_url`` disables.
    - ``embedding_model`` — see the module docstring's coupling (2).
    - ``client`` / ``http`` — injected doubles for tests.
    """

    qdrant_url: str
    litellm_url: str
    litellm_api_key: str = ""
    embedding_model: str = DEFAULT_FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL
    client: Any | None = None
    http: Any | None = None
    _owns_client: bool = field(init=False, default=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.client is None and self.qdrant_url:
            self.client = AsyncQdrantClient(url=self.qdrant_url)
            self._owns_client = True

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """True when both halves of the search are configured.

        Both are required and neither is sufficient: without Qdrant there is
        nothing to search, and without the embeddings gateway there is no
        query vector to search WITH. Half-enabled would mean a node that
        fails deep inside instead of at its own precondition.
        """
        return self.client is not None and bool(self.litellm_url)

    @staticmethod
    def chunks_collection(org_id: str) -> str:
        """Return the files-svc per-tenant chunk collection name.

        files-svc owns and writes it; this vertical only reads. The name MUST
        match ``files_svc.worker.qdrant_client.Qdrant.chunks_collection`` —
        range-svc's ``files_chunks_collection`` carries the same warning.
        """
        return f"files_chunks_{org_id}"

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the Qdrant client, but only if this instance opened it."""
        if self._owns_client and self.client is not None:
            await self.client.close()

    async def embed_query(self, query: str) -> list[float]:
        """Embed ``query`` through the LiteLLM gateway.

        Mirrors ``files_svc.worker.embedding.Embedder.embed_text`` — same
        endpoint, same request shape — because the two must produce vectors in
        the same space to be comparable at all.
        """
        if not self.litellm_url:
            raise FilesChunkSearchError(
                "the embeddings gateway is not configured on this worker (LITELLM_URL)"
            )
        text = query[:MAX_QUERY_CHARS]
        headers = (
            {"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.litellm_api_key}"} if self.litellm_api_key else {}
        )
        payload = {"model": self.embedding_model, "input": text}
        try:
            if self.http is not None:
                resp = await self.http.post(
                    f"{self.litellm_url.rstrip('/')}/embeddings",
                    headers=headers,
                    json=payload,
                    timeout=_EMBED_TIMEOUT_S,
                )
            else:
                async with httpx.AsyncClient() as http:
                    resp = await http.post(
                        f"{self.litellm_url.rstrip('/')}/embeddings",
                        headers=headers,
                        json=payload,
                        timeout=_EMBED_TIMEOUT_S,
                    )
            resp.raise_for_status()
            body = resp.json()
            return [float(v) for v in body["data"][0]["embedding"]]
        except FilesChunkSearchError:
            raise
        except (httpx.HTTPError, KeyError, IndexError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
            raise FilesChunkSearchError(f"embedding the query failed: {exc}") from exc

    async def search(
        self,
        *,
        org_id: str,
        query: str,
        document_ids: list[str],
        limit: int,
    ) -> list[ChunkHit]:
        """Return the chunks nearest ``query``, most similar first.

        ``document_ids`` scopes the search — see the module docstring on why
        that is the corpus filter. An EMPTY list returns no hits without
        embedding anything: there is nothing to search, and spending an
        embedding call to prove it would be waste. Same shortcut range-svc
        takes.

        A collection that does not exist yet (nothing in the corpus has
        finished ingesting) returns an empty list rather than raising — see
        :class:`FilesChunkSearchError`'s docstring.
        """
        if not document_ids:
            return []
        if not self.enabled:
            raise FilesChunkSearchError(
                "document search is not configured on this worker (QDRANT_URL / LITELLM_URL)"
            )
        assert self.client is not None  # narrowed by `enabled`

        vector = await self.embed_query(query)
        try:
            results = await self.client.search(
                collection_name=self.chunks_collection(org_id),
                query_vector=vector,
                query_filter=models.Filter(
                    must=[
                        models.FieldCondition(
                            key="document_id",
                            match=models.MatchAny(any=list(document_ids)),
                        )
                    ]
                ),
                limit=max(1, limit),
                with_payload=True,
            )
        except Exception:
            # The collection legitimately may not exist: a corpus whose
            # documents have not been ingested yet has no points and therefore
            # no collection. Qdrant answers that with a 404-shaped error, and
            # the client's exception family is wide enough that catching the
            # specific type would be brittle. An empty result is the honest
            # answer to "search a corpus with nothing indexed in it", and the
            # executor separately reports ingest status so this does not look
            # like a silent failure. Same reasoning (and same broad catch) as
            # range-svc's `search_chunks_by_vector`.
            return []

        hits: list[ChunkHit] = []
        for point in results:
            payload = getattr(point, "payload", None) or {}
            text = payload.get("text")
            if not text:
                # A point written before `upsert_chunk` carried text (the
                # field is additive and back-compat) has nothing to show.
                continue
            hits.append(
                ChunkHit(
                    document_id=str(payload.get("document_id", "")),
                    text=str(text),
                    score=float(getattr(point, "score", 0.0) or 0.0),
                )
            )
        return hits


__all__ = [
    "DEFAULT_FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL",
    "MAX_QUERY_CHARS",
    "ChunkHit",
    "FilesChunkSearch",
    "FilesChunkSearchError",
]

"""Tabular document parse/serialize for the two Table nodes (#1411 / #1412).

Files & Data node family (#1407). Read the design doc's §6 first: "a table is
a tabular document in a Files corpus" is the epic's explicit re-pointing
decision, taken because there is no Tables vertical and the epic's own parity
audit left the choice open. This module is where that decision becomes code.

Pure functions over text — no I/O, no gRPC, no config. The executors own the
Files hop; this module owns the format.

Three choices worth stating:

**The delimiter comes from the MIME type, never from sniffing the bytes.**
``text/tab-separated-values`` is a tab; everything else in
``nodes.filesdata.TABULAR_MIME_TYPES`` is a comma. ``csv.Sniffer`` guesses
wrong on a single-column file (no delimiter to find) and on a comma-free
one-column CSV it can pick a character that appears inside the data. A wrong
guess here does not fail — it silently produces a differently-shaped table,
which is the worst outcome of the three.

**The header row IS the schema.** That is what makes #1412's "schema mismatch
between content and table columns shows an error on the result handle (not a
crash)" a real check rather than a formality: :func:`schema_mismatch` compares
sets, so a row with an unknown column or a missing one is caught before
anything is written.

**The row cap is enforced DURING the read.** :func:`parse_rows` stops pulling
from the reader once ``limit`` rows are in hand rather than slicing afterwards,
so returning 100 rows from a very large CSV does not first materialize the
whole thing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

#: MIME type whose values are tab-separated. Everything else in
#: `nodes.filesdata.TABULAR_MIME_TYPES` is comma-separated.
TSV_MIME_TYPE = "text/tab-separated-values"

#: The MIME type a table this family CREATES is written as. Deliberately
#: `text/csv` even when appending to a `.tsv`: see `serialize_rows`.
CSV_MIME_TYPE = "text/csv"


class TabularError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a document cannot be read as a table, or rows cannot be
    written to one.

    Every executor converts this into a ``NodeExecutionError`` so a malformed
    table fails ONE node with a reason naming the actual problem.
    """


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Table:
    """A parsed tabular document."""

    #: The header row, in FILE order. Order matters and a list of dicts does
    #: not preserve it, which is why `get_from_table` publishes `columns`
    #: separately: a downstream node writing these rows back needs it.
    columns: tuple[str, ...]
    rows: tuple[dict[str, str], ...]
    #: True when the file held more rows than the caller's limit. NOT an
    #: error — `get_from_table` publishes it so a truncated read is visible
    #: rather than looking like the whole table.
    truncated: bool


def delimiter_for(mime_type: str) -> str:
    """Return the field delimiter for ``mime_type``. See the module docstring
    on why this is not sniffed."""
    return "\t" if mime_type.strip().lower().startswith(TSV_MIME_TYPE) else ","


def decode(content: bytes) -> str:
    """Decode table bytes as UTF-8, tolerating a BOM.

    ``utf-8-sig`` rather than ``utf-8``: a CSV exported from Excel starts with
    a BOM, and under plain utf-8 that BOM becomes part of the FIRST COLUMN'S
    NAME (``"\\ufeffid"`` instead of ``"id"``). Every subsequent lookup by
    column name then misses, and #1412's schema check would reject a table
    against its own header. Errors are surfaced, never replaced: a table this
    module cannot decode is a table the node must fail on, not one to guess at.
    """
    try:
        return content.decode("utf-8-sig")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise TabularError(
            "the selected table is not UTF-8 text — pick a CSV or TSV document"
        ) from exc


def parse_table(content: bytes, *, mime_type: str, limit: int) -> Table:
    """Parse ``content`` as a table, returning at most ``limit`` rows.

    An empty document raises: a table with no header has no schema, and every
    caller of this function needs one (``get_from_table`` to publish
    ``columns``, ``save_to_table`` to validate against). A header-only
    document is fine and yields zero rows.
    """
    text = decode(content)
    reader = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text), delimiter=delimiter_for(mime_type))
    fieldnames = reader.fieldnames
    if not fieldnames:
        raise TabularError("the selected table is empty — it has no header row")
    columns = tuple(str(name) for name in fieldnames)

    rows: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    truncated = False
    capped = max(0, limit)
    for raw in reader:
        if len(rows) >= capped:
            # One row beyond the cap is enough to know the file held more; do
            # not keep reading (see the module docstring).
            truncated = True
            break
        # `DictReader` yields None for a short row's missing trailing cells and
        # collects extras under the `None` key. Normalize both: a table read is
        # not the place to fail on a ragged CSV, and a downstream node reading
        # `row["notes"]` should get "" rather than None.
        rows.append({col: ("" if raw.get(col) is None else str(raw.get(col))) for col in columns})
    return Table(columns=columns, rows=tuple(rows), truncated=truncated)


def coerce_rows(value: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Coerce an upstream node's output into a list of row dicts.

    Accepts what the canvas actually produces at this seam, in the order it is
    most likely to arrive:

    - a list of objects — the ordinary case (``get_from_table``'s own ``rows``,
      a ``filter`` node's output);
    - a single object — a one-row write, which every node emitting a record
      produces;
    - a JSON string of either — what an ``http_request`` body or an AI node's
      text output looks like.

    Raises :class:`TabularError` on anything else, naming what arrived. A
    scalar or a list of scalars has no column names and so cannot become a
    row, and guessing one ("value") would write a table nobody asked for.
    """
    if isinstance(value, str):
        import json

        try:
            value = json.loads(value)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise TabularError(
                "the content wired into this node is text, not table rows — "
                "connect a node that emits objects, or JSON describing them"
            ) from exc
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return [dict(value)]
    if isinstance(value, list):
        if not value:
            return []
        bad = next((r for r in value if not isinstance(r, dict)), None)
        if bad is not None:
            raise TabularError(
                f"table rows must be objects with named columns, got {type(bad).__name__}"
            )
        return [dict(r) for r in value]

        f"table rows must be an object or a list of objects, got {type(value).__name__}"
    )


def schema_mismatch(columns: tuple[str, ...], rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
    """Return a human-readable mismatch description, or ``""`` when the rows
    fit ``columns``.

    #1412's acceptance criterion is that a mismatch "shows an error on the
    result handle (not a crash)", so this returns a MESSAGE rather than
    raising — the caller decides that it is a node failure, and the message it
    fails with names the specific columns involved rather than saying
    "schema mismatch".

    A row is allowed to OMIT a column (the cell is written empty); it is not
    allowed to introduce one, because a new column would silently not be
    written and the run would report success having dropped data.
    """
    known = set(columns)
    unknown: list[str] = []
    for row in rows:
        for key in row:
            name = str(key)
            if name not in known and name not in unknown:
                unknown.append(name)
    if not unknown:
        return ""
    return (
        f"the incoming rows have {len(unknown)} column(s) the table does not: "
        f"{', '.join(sorted(unknown))}. The table's columns are: {', '.join(columns)}"
    )


def serialize_rows(columns: tuple[str, ...], rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> bytes:
    """Render ``rows`` as a UTF-8 CSV with ``columns`` as the header.

    ``CSV_MIME_TYPE``, so the change is visible in the document's own metadata
    rather than hidden inside bytes that still claim to be tab-separated.

    ``QUOTE_MINIMAL`` with ``\\r\\n`` line endings — RFC 4180, and what
    ``csv.writer`` defaults to. A value containing the delimiter, a quote or a
    newline is quoted, so a round trip through :func:`parse_table` is lossless.

    Values are stringified with ``str``, and ``None`` becomes an empty cell
    rather than the literal text "None".
    """
    buf = io.StringIO(newline="")
    writer = csv.DictWriter(
        buf,
        fieldnames=list(columns),
        # A key not in `columns` would raise ValueError mid-write, leaving a
        # partial file. `schema_mismatch` is what catches that BEFORE the
        # write, so this is defence in depth: ignore rather than explode.
        extrasaction="ignore",
        lineterminator="\r\n",
    )
    writer.writeheader()
    for row in rows:
        writer.writerow(
            {col: ("" if row.get(col) is None else str(row.get(col))) for col in columns}

    return buf.getvalue().encode("utf-8")


def columns_from_rows(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Derive a header for a NEW table from its first rows.

    First-seen order across every row, not just the first: two rows from a
    branchy graph can legitimately carry different key sets, and taking only
    the first row's keys would drop the rest without saying so (which
    :func:`schema_mismatch` exists to prevent on the append path). Union in
    encounter order keeps the common case — uniform rows — reading exactly as
    the author wrote it.
    """
    columns: list[str] = []
    for row in rows:
        for key in row:
            name = str(key)
            if name not in columns:
                columns.append(name)
    return tuple(columns)

    "delimiter_for",
    "parse_table",
    "schema_mismatch",
    "serialize_rows",
]

here. What differs is written down below, because none of it is inferable
from the client code.

**Who calls.** ``workflow-svc-worker``, not workflow-svc. A workflow run is
dispatched over JetStream long after the user who started it went away, so
the worker mints its own OIDC ``client_credentials`` token
(:mod:`workflow_svc.serviceauth`, shared with the Dialogue hop and the Media
family's studio-svc hop).

**The four gates, as they apply here:**

1. *mTLS* — dials via ``omnicore_svc_runtime.mtls.build_channel``.
2. *aud* — the ``workflow-svc-worker`` realm client gains an
   ``audience-files-svc-via-workflow-svc-worker`` protocol mapper, so its
   token is minted with ``aud=[workflow-svc, studio-svc, dialogue-svc,
   files-svc]``. pyjwt treats a multi-valued ``aud`` as a membership test, so
   one token still serves every target.
3. *azp* — ``FILES_SVC_ALLOWED_AZP`` (platform/compose/files-svc.yml) gains
   ``workflow-svc-worker``.
4. *tenant* — a ``client_credentials`` token carries no ``org_id``. The
   ``tenant:any`` realm role (already granted to
   ``service-account-workflow-svc-worker`` for the Dialogue hop) is what lets
   files-svc's interceptor ADOPT ``x-tenant-id`` as the caller's effective
   org. Without the role, files-svc rejects a blank-org_id token that names a
   tenant — that is F31, and it stays intact for every token lacking the
   grant.

**A fifth thing, specific to this hop: the actor.** Every call here forwards
``x-user-id`` carrying ``workflow.executions.created_by`` — the UUID of the
person who STARTED the run — and not the service account. Attributing a write
to the initiator is the honest answer to "who saved this file", and the
literal string ``workflow-svc-worker`` (what ``NodeContext.user_id`` carries)
could not satisfy ``files.documents.uploaded_by``, which is ``UUID NOT NULL``.
``NodeContext.initiator_user_id`` exists for exactly this.

**files-svc reads that header as of #2922, so the gate is effective.** It
adopts ``x-user-id`` as the acting user for a caller holding ``tenant:any``,
symmetrically with how it already adopts ``x-tenant-id``, and validates the
adopted id against its own org-membership projection. Two consequences, both
of which reverse decisions #2918 made:

1. Attribution lands on the initiator. ``documents.uploaded_by`` and
   ``deleted_by`` name the person whose run wrote or superseded the document,

2. A run reads what the initiator reads, PRIVATE corpora included — so

"""FilesClient — workflow-svc-worker's outbound gRPC client to files-svc.

Files & Data node family (#1407). Read :mod:`workflow_svc.files`'s package
docstring first: it holds the five-gate auth posture (four shared with the
Dialogue hop, plus the initiator-actor rule) and the reason bytes do not
travel over gRPC. None of that is inferable from this file alone.

Scope is exactly what the five nodes need, and no more:

- ``get_document`` — metadata only. ``load_document`` calls it BEFORE
  streaming so an oversized document costs one RPC instead of 50 MB of
  transfer (design §5).
- ``list_documents`` — every document in a corpus, paged to exhaustion.
  This is what scopes ``document_query`` to a corpus: the Qdrant chunk payload
  carries a ``document_id`` but no ``corpus_id``, so the corpus has to be
  turned into a document-id set first (design §4).
- ``get_raw_file`` — the only raw-bytes surface files-svc has.
- ``save_document`` — MinIO put + ``Upload``, with the compensating delete.
- ``trash_document`` — the second half of Save to Table's append (design
  §6.4). Trash, never Purge: a mis-wired workflow must be undoable from the
  Files UI.

``addr=""`` (or no token source) returns a DISABLED client: every method
raises :class:`FilesClientError` without touching the network.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Protocol

import grpc
from omnicore.files.corpus.v1 import corpus_pb2, corpus_pb2_grpc
from omnicore.files.document.v1 import document_pb2, document_pb2_grpc
from omnicore_svc_runtime.mtls import MTLSConfig, build_channel

#: Bound every unary RPC. A hung files-svc must not pin the worker on one
#: node for longer than the engine's own 30 s per-node dispatch timeout, which
#: would make the node's failure read as an engine timeout instead of a Files
#: one.
_UNARY_TIMEOUT_S = 20.0

#: Streaming a document can legitimately take longer than a unary read — up to
#: `MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES` of it — but still has to fit inside the engine's
#: per-node budget, so this is deliberately under it.
_RAW_FILE_TIMEOUT_S = 25.0

#: `DocumentService.List` caps `limit` at 200 server-side (document.proto). Ask
#: for the cap rather than the default 50 so a large corpus costs a quarter of
#: the round trips.
_LIST_PAGE_SIZE = 200

#: Hard stop on the paging loop in `list_documents`. A corpus with more
#: documents than this cannot be searched exhaustively in one node run, and
#: silently searching a prefix would make `document_query` quietly wrong on
#: big corpora. The caller surfaces the truncation instead.
_MAX_LIST_PAGES = 50


class FilesClientError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when the Files hop cannot be completed.

    Covers "this client was never configured", "files-svc answered with an
    error", and "the object store rejected the write". Every executor converts
    it into a ``NodeExecutionError`` so the run records ONE failed node rather
    than a crashed worker.
    """


#: Appended to a NOT_FOUND from files-svc, which is genuinely ambiguous here
#: and was actively misleading in review.
#:
#: files-svc gates every client-facing document read on
#: ``_CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE`` — ``visibility = 'TEAM' OR created_by =
#: app.current_user_id`` — so a document in a collection the acting user did
#: not create and that is not shared is indistinguishable from a deleted one:
#: both answer NOT_FOUND.
#:
#: #2922 narrowed which collections that covers but did not remove the
#: ambiguity. files-svc now binds ``app.current_user_id`` from the
#: ``x-user-id`` this client forwards, so the acting user is the run's
#: initiator and their OWN private collections are readable. Someone ELSE's
#: private collection still is not — reachable through a canvas saved by a
#: colleague, a shared workflow, or a direct API call — and a bare "document
#: not found" would still send an operator looking for a deletion that never
#: happened.
_NOT_FOUND_HINT = (
    " — either it was deleted, or it lives in a collection you cannot open: a "
    "run reads as the person who started it, so another user's private "
    "collection is invisible to it. Documents a shared workflow reads should "
    "be in a shared (TEAM) collection."
)


#: Appended when a WRITE is rejected because its target corpus is not visible.
#:
#: The write path expresses the same invisibility as the read path but with a
#: different status and a worse message. ``DocumentService.Upload`` pre-checks
#: ``GET_CORPUS`` — which carries the same ``_CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE`` — and
#: aborts FAILED_PRECONDITION with ``corpus_id <uuid> not found in this org``.
#: That sentence is wrong from the operator's side whenever the cause is
#: visibility: the collection IS in their org.
#:
#: Found while re-checking the read-path fix from review on PR #2918. The same
#: defect, one status code over. Since #2922 the initiator's own private
#: collections are writable, so what reaches here is a collection belonging to
#: someone else — which the wording now says.
_CORPUS_NOT_WRITABLE_HINT = (
    " — if that collection exists but belongs to another user and is private, "
    "a run cannot write to it: a run acts as the person who started it. Save "
    "to your own collection or a shared (TEAM) one."
)


def _rpc_message(action: str, exc: grpc.aio.AioRpcError) -> str:
    """Render one failed RPC as a node-failure reason.

    NOT_FOUND gets :data:`_NOT_FOUND_HINT`; every other code speaks for itself
    and is passed through unchanged rather than being second-guessed.
    """
    detail = exc.details() or exc.code().name
    if exc.code() is grpc.StatusCode.NOT_FOUND:
        return f"{action}: {detail}{_NOT_FOUND_HINT}"
    return f"{action}: {detail}"


def _upload_message(exc: grpc.aio.AioRpcError) -> str:
    """Render a failed ``Upload`` as a node-failure reason.

    Separate from :func:`_rpc_message` because the ambiguity is different on
    this path: files-svc answers FAILED_PRECONDITION (not NOT_FOUND) for a
    corpus the caller cannot see, so the read hint would never fire and the
    write hint must not leak onto unrelated preconditions. Only that one code
    is decorated; everything else passes through.
    """
    detail = exc.details() or exc.code().name
    if exc.code() is grpc.StatusCode.FAILED_PRECONDITION:
        return f"document upload failed: {detail}{_CORPUS_NOT_WRITABLE_HINT}"
    return f"document upload failed: {detail}"


class TokenSourceLike(Protocol):
    """Structural type for the injected token source (ServiceAccountTokenSource
    in production; a fake in tests)."""

    async def get_token(self) -> str: ...


class ObjectStoreLike(Protocol):
    """The two S3 operations ``save_document`` needs.

    A Protocol rather than a concrete aiobotocore client so tests inject a
    double without a live MinIO, and so the compensating-delete path is
    exercisable. Matches aiobotocore's own async client surface.
    """

    async def put_object(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Any: ...
    async def delete_object(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Any: ...


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class DocumentMeta:
    """The subset of ``files.document.v1.Document`` this family reads."""

    id: str
    filename: str
    mime_type: str
    size_bytes: int
    corpus_id: str
    #: Pipeline state of the document's most recent ingest job — "complete",
    #: "failed", one of the in-flight states, or "" when no job exists.
    #: `document_query` reports it so a corpus that has not finished ingesting
    #: explains its own empty result set instead of looking broken.
    ingest_status: str


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class UploadResult:
    """What ``save_document`` learned from files-svc about the new row."""

    document_id: str
    filename: str
    mime_type: str
    size_bytes: int
    #: files-svc enqueues parse/chunk/embed on Upload and returns the job id.
    #: Carried through to the node's `result` because saving a document is
    #: only the START of ingest — a workflow that saves then queries needs
    #: this to know when the document became searchable.
    ingest_job_id: str


def _mtls_cfg_from_env() -> MTLSConfig:
    """Same ``MTLS_*_FILE`` env vars the inbound server reads (P0-05) — this is
    the outbound half of the same east-west posture."""
    return MTLSConfig(
        os.environ.get("MTLS_CERT_FILE", ""),
        os.environ.get("MTLS_KEY_FILE", ""),
        os.environ.get("MTLS_CA_FILE", ""),
    )


def _document_meta(doc: Any) -> DocumentMeta:
    """Map a wire ``Document`` onto :class:`DocumentMeta`."""
    return DocumentMeta(
        id=str(doc.id),
        filename=str(doc.filename),
        mime_type=str(doc.mime_type),
        size_bytes=int(doc.size_bytes),
        corpus_id=str(doc.corpus_id),
        ingest_status=str(doc.ingest_status),
    )


@dataclass(slots=True)
class FilesClient:
    """Thin wrapper around files-svc's ``DocumentServiceStub`` plus the object
    store its Upload contract requires the caller to write to.

    Parameters:
    - ``addr`` — files-svc gRPC dial target (e.g. ``"files-svc:50051"``).
      Empty disables the client.
    - ``token_source`` — mints the bearer JWT files-svc's AuthInterceptor
      requires on every RPC. ``None`` disables the client.
    - ``bucket`` — the files-svc MinIO bucket. Blank disables WRITES only:
      reads still work, and `save_to_file` fails that one node with a reason
      naming the missing config.
    - ``object_store`` — an :class:`ObjectStoreLike`. ``None`` likewise
      disables writes only.
    - ``stub`` — optional injected ``DocumentServiceStub``-shaped double.
    """

    addr: str
    token_source: TokenSourceLike | None
    bucket: str = ""
    object_store: ObjectStoreLike | None = None
    stub: Any | None = None
    #: ``CorpusServiceStub``, used ONLY by :meth:`corpus_is_readable`. Shares
    #: the one channel; injectable separately so a test can drive the probe
    #: without a document stub.
    corpus_stub: Any | None = None
    _channel: grpc.aio.Channel | None = field(init=False, default=None)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.stub is None and self.addr:
            self._channel, _ = build_channel(self.addr, _mtls_cfg_from_env())
            self.stub = document_pb2_grpc.DocumentServiceStub(self._channel)  # type: ignore[no-untyped-call]
            if self.corpus_stub is None:
                self.corpus_stub = corpus_pb2_grpc.CorpusServiceStub(self._channel)  # type: ignore[no-untyped-call]

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """True when a stub AND a token source are both configured.

        Both halves are required: an addr with no token source could only ever
        produce UNAUTHENTICATED, and a token source with no addr has nowhere to
        send it. Refusing to half-enable keeps this an honest single predicate.
        """
        return self.stub is not None and self.token_source is not None

    @property
    def writable(self) -> bool:
        """True when this client can also SAVE — i.e. it has somewhere to put
        the bytes ``Upload`` will then register.

        Deliberately separate from :attr:`enabled`: a worker configured for
        files-svc but not for MinIO can still run every read node, and only
        `save_to_file` / `save_to_table` need to fail.
        """
        return self.enabled and bool(self.bucket) and self.object_store is not None

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the gRPC channel and the token source's HTTP client."""

            await self._channel.close()
        if self.token_source is not None:
            closer = getattr(self.token_source, "close", None)
            if closer is not None:
                await closer()

    async def _metadata(self, *, org_id: str, user_id: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
        """Build the outbound metadata for one RPC.

        ``x-tenant-id`` is the tenant this run belongs to; files-svc ADOPTS it
        as the caller's effective org because the worker's token carries the
        ``tenant:any`` grant and no ``org_id`` of its own.

        ``x-user-id`` is the UUID of the person who STARTED the run, not the
        service account. files-svc ADOPTS it as the acting user under the same
        ``tenant:any`` grant, so everything it derives from the acting user
        follows this value: ``documents.uploaded_by``, ``deleted_by``, and the
        ``app.current_user_id`` GUC that decides corpus visibility.

        That adoption is #2922, and it is what makes this header load-bearing
        rather than decorative. Before it, files-svc derived the acting user
        from the token SUBJECT and ignored this header entirely, so every
        run-authored document was owned by the worker's service account and a
        run could read ``TEAM`` corpora only. Both halves are now the
        initiator's.

        Sending a ``x-user-id`` that is not a member of ``org_id`` is
        PERMISSION_DENIED at files-svc, not a silent fallback to the service
        account — so pass ``executions.created_by``, never
        ``NodeContext.user_id`` (the service-account name).
        """
        if self.token_source is None:  # pragma: no cover - guarded by `enabled`
            raise FilesClientError("files client is not configured")
        token = await self.token_source.get_token()
        metadata = [
            ("authorization", f"Bearer {token}"),
            ("x-tenant-id", org_id),
            ("x-actor-type", "service"),
        ]
        if user_id:
            metadata.append(("x-user-id", user_id))
        return metadata

    def _require_enabled(self) -> None:
        if not self.enabled:
            raise FilesClientError(
                "the Files integration is not configured on this worker "
                "(FILES_SVC_ADDR / WORKFLOW_SVC_WORKER_CLIENT_SECRET)"
            )

    async def get_document(self, document_id: str, *, org_id: str, user_id: str) -> DocumentMeta:
        """Fetch one document's metadata. Raises on a missing/forbidden id."""
        self._require_enabled()
        assert self.stub is not None  # narrowed by `enabled`
        metadata = await self._metadata(org_id=org_id, user_id=user_id)
        try:
            resp = await self.stub.Get(
                document_pb2.GetRequest(document_id=document_id),
                metadata=metadata,
                timeout=_UNARY_TIMEOUT_S,
            )
        except grpc.aio.AioRpcError as exc:
            raise FilesClientError(_rpc_message("document lookup failed", exc)) from exc
        return _document_meta(resp.document)

    async def list_documents(
        self,
        corpus_id: str,
        *,
        org_id: str,
        user_id: str,
        max_pages: int = _MAX_LIST_PAGES,
    ) -> tuple[list[DocumentMeta], bool]:
        """Page every document in a corpus, across folders.

        ``all_folders=True`` deliberately: a corpus-wide search must not be
        silently limited to corpus-root documents, which is what the
        ``folder_id``-unset default means (see document.proto's ListRequest).

        Returns ``(documents, truncated)``. ``truncated`` is True when
        ``max_pages`` was exhausted with a cursor still outstanding — the
        caller surfaces it rather than searching a prefix and reporting a
        complete answer.

        out: list[DocumentMeta] = []

                    document_pb2.ListRequest(
                        corpus_id=corpus_id,
                        cursor=cursor,
                        limit=_LIST_PAGE_SIZE,
                        all_folders=True,
                    ),
                    metadata=metadata,

                raise FilesClientError(_rpc_message("document list failed", exc)) from exc
            out.extend(_document_meta(d) for d in resp.documents)

    async def get_raw_file(
        self, document_id: str, *, org_id: str, user_id: str
    ) -> tuple[bytes, str, str]:
        """Stream a document's full raw bytes.

        Returns ``(data, mime_type, filename)``. The first frame of the stream
        is metadata and every later frame is a data chunk — see
        ``GetRawFileResponse``'s ``oneof``.

        (if useless) table, and the caller is better placed to decide whether
        emptiness matters than this transport wrapper is.

        filename = ""
        try:
            call = self.stub.GetRawFile(
                document_pb2.GetRawFileRequest(document_id=document_id),
                metadata=metadata,
                timeout=_RAW_FILE_TIMEOUT_S,
            )
            async for frame in call:
                if frame.WhichOneof("frame") == "metadata":
                    mime_type = str(frame.metadata.mime_type)
                    filename = str(frame.metadata.filename)
                else:
                    chunks.append(frame.data)
        except grpc.aio.AioRpcError as exc:
            # Same NOT_FOUND ambiguity as the unary reads above — a document in
            # a PRIVATE collection and a deleted one are indistinguishable from
            # here.
            raise FilesClientError(_rpc_message("document download failed", exc)) from exc
        except grpc.RpcError as exc:
            # Broader net for a streaming call: not every failure on this path
            # carries a status code (a transport drop mid-stream does not), so
            # this arm keeps the raw repr rather than pretending to classify it.
            raise FilesClientError(f"document download failed: {exc}") from exc
        return b"".join(chunks), mime_type, filename

    async def corpus_is_readable(self, corpus_id: str, *, org_id: str, user_id: str) -> bool:
        """Can a workflow RUN read this collection at all?

        Exists because "this collection is empty" and "this collection is
        invisible to me" are the same answer from ``DocumentService.List``:
        files-svc gates it on ``_CORPUS_VISIBLE_PREDICATE`` but returns an
        EMPTY LIST rather than an error, so an unreadable corpus looks exactly
        like an empty one. Without this, ``document_query`` reported "no
        results" for a collection the run was never allowed to see — the
        quietest failure of the three in this family.

"""MinioObjectStore — the object-store half of the Files save path (#1407).

``DocumentService.Upload`` takes a bucket-relative object KEY and never
bytes: "files stream through files-bff to MinIO; this RPC just receives the
metadata + MinIO object key" (document.proto). So a caller that wants to save
content must put the object itself first, which is exactly what files-bff's
Upload handler does. :class:`MinioObjectStore` is the workflow worker's half
of that same contract, and nothing more — two operations, both used only by
``save_to_file`` and ``save_to_table``.

Modelled directly on ``files_svc.minio_client.MinIOClient``, including the
part that is easy to get wrong: ``aiobotocore``'s ``create_client`` returns an
async CONTEXT MANAGER, not a client, so its ``__aenter__``/``__aexit__`` have
to be driven explicitly to keep one client alive across many calls. Opening a
fresh client per call would turn a workflow that writes N files into N TLS
connection establishments.

The client is opened LAZILY, on first use, for two reasons: the factory that
constructs this object is synchronous (an executor is a module-level function
with no async init point), and a worker whose runs never reach a save node
should never open an S3 session at all.

``signature_version="s3v4"`` + path-style addressing mirror files-svc's own
config. MinIO requires path style — virtual-host addressing would resolve
``<bucket>.minio`` as a hostname, which does not exist on the compose network.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any


@dataclass
class MinioObjectStore:
    """Long-lived async S3 client exposing just ``put_object`` / ``delete_object``.

    Satisfies :class:`workflow_svc.files.client.ObjectStoreLike` structurally,
    so ``FilesClient`` depends on the two methods rather than on aiobotocore.
    """

    endpoint_url: str
    access_key: str
    secret_key: str
    secure: bool = False
    region: str = "us-east-1"
    _session: Any = field(default=None, init=False, repr=False)
    _client_cm: Any = field(default=None, init=False, repr=False)
    _client: Any = field(default=None, init=False, repr=False)

    async def _ensure_client(self) -> Any:
        """Open the underlying aiobotocore client on first use."""
        if self._client is not None:
            return self._client
        import aiobotocore.session
        from botocore.config import Config

        if self._session is None:
            self._session = aiobotocore.session.get_session()
        # See the module docstring: this is an async context manager, driven
        # explicitly so one client survives many calls and is torn down in
        # `close()`.
        self._client_cm = self._session.create_client(
            "s3",
            endpoint_url=self.endpoint_url,
            aws_access_key_id=self.access_key,
            aws_secret_access_key=self.secret_key,
            use_ssl=self.secure,
            # MinIO ignores the region but botocore requires one to sign.
            region_name=self.region,
            config=Config(
                signature_version="s3v4",
                s3={"addressing_style": "path"},
            ),
        )
        self._client = await self._client_cm.__aenter__()
        return self._client

    async def put_object(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        """Write one object. Keyword arguments are botocore's own."""
        s3 = await self._ensure_client()
        return await s3.put_object(**kwargs)

    async def delete_object(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        """Delete one object — the compensating half of a rejected upload."""
        s3 = await self._ensure_client()
        return await s3.delete_object(**kwargs)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Tear the client down. Idempotent; safe on a never-opened store."""
        if self._client_cm is not None:
            await self._client_cm.__aexit__(None, None, None)
        self._client_cm = None
        self._client = None

"""FilesChunkSearch — semantic search over the chunk collection files-svc writes.

Files & Data node family (#1407), backing the Document Query node (#1408).
Read the design doc's §4 before changing this: the choice to read Qdrant
rather than call files-svc is the load-bearing decision of the epic, and it
is not obvious from here that it is a sanctioned pattern rather than a
shortcut.

The short version. files-svc ingests, chunks and embeds documents into a
per-tenant Qdrant collection, and exposes **no search RPC at all** — the only
``search_documents`` in the platform is a declared tool name in
``agents-svc/internal/registry`` with ``JSONSchema: "{}"`` and no
implementation. What files-svc DOES do is store the chunk text in the Qdrant
point payload specifically so other verticals can read it: see
``files_svc.worker.qdrant_client.upsert_chunk``, whose docstring says the text
is there "so that cross-vertical readers (range-svc RAG retrieval) can pull
grounding text straight from Qdrant with no files-svc gRPC hop". range-svc's
``embedding/qdrant_client.search_chunks_by_vector`` is that reader, and calls
it "the architecture-blessed cross-vertical read; range-svc never calls
files-svc gRPC". This module is the second such reader.

**files-svc owns and writes this collection; workflow-svc only reads it.**
Nothing here creates, upserts into or deletes from it, and nothing should.

Two couplings this file cannot avoid and therefore names loudly:

1. **The collection name** must match
   ``files_svc.worker.qdrant_client.Qdrant.chunks_collection`` exactly.
2. **The embedding model** must be the one files-svc embedded the chunks with,
   or the query lands in a different vector space and retrieval returns noise
   that *looks* like results. ``WORKFLOW_FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL`` therefore
   defaults to files-svc's own ``FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL`` default
   (``nomic-embed-text:latest``) — NOT to workflow's gen-model pin. range-svc
   carries the identical ``RANGE_FILES_EMBEDDING_MODEL`` for the identical
   reason.

payload carries ``org_id``, ``chunk_id``, ``document_id`` and ``text`` — no
``corpus_id``. So the caller resolves the corpus to its document ids (via
``FilesClient.list_documents``) and this module filters ``MatchAny`` over
them, exactly as range-svc filters to a run's attached documents.
